claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about your situation and your children.

Let me start with a few questions:

**How many children do you have that you're inquiring about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK, and do you live with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. But no, Alex doesn't live with me actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex lives with someone else, but you're still interested in potentially claiming Child Benefit for him.

**Are you making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep, such as money for his food, clothes, pocket money, or housing? If so, how much are you contributing and how often?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently contributing financially to Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's an important detail.

Just to make sure I have the full picture, **is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex currently?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, the person he lives with is already claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the rules, here's the situation:

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child lives with someone else, you can normally get Child Benefit for 8 weeks after the child goes to live with them (if nobody else claims). However, it can continue for longer **only if you make financial contributions towards the child's upkeep** at the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment.

In your case:
- Alex lives with someone else
- That person is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- You are not making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep

Since someone else is already receiving Child Benefit for Alex and you're not contributing financially to his upkeep, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time**.

However, if your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you start making regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep—you may want to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your options further.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
